summary: Task 1 introduces two Java POJOs (Trigger.java, Funnel.java) and three unit test files — a pure domain/persistence-model change with no application attack surface. OWASP Top 10 analysis found no issues: (1) The unique partial index uses '$exists: true' which correctly excludes null values, preventing null-collision attacks and preserving the on_start uniqueness invariant at the DB level — this cannot be bypassed. (2) No mass-assignment surface: both POJOs are plain Java with no Spring MVC binding, no Jackson annotations, and no @RequestBody — DTO binding with @JsonIgnoreProperties is deferred to Task 3 as designed. (3) No injection surface: no queries, no EL/SPEL, no JNDI, no custom deserializers — fields are plain String and List<String>; MongoDB queries are constructed in the repository layer (Task 2). (4) No PII in field names or values. (5) No secrets or hardcoded credentials — the static block 'active' literal is a defensive invariant assertion, not a secret. (6) No deserialization risk: no @JsonTypeInfo, no _class discriminator, statically-typed List<Trigger> field avoids gadget chain exposure. (7) The empty-string onStartTriggerValue ('') correctly participates in the unique index (it is $exists: true in MongoDB), which is the intended behavior for bare /start funnels. Approved with zero findings.
